1 INTRODUCTION
1.1 GENERAL
This statistical analysis plan (SAP) describes the statistical methods to be used during the reporting and
analyses of data collected under Protocol P-VCNA-003 (Simbec-Orion study 35667) sponsored by VCN
Biosciences S.L., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Theriva Biologics, Inc., and should be read in conjunction
with the study protocol and case report form (CRF).
This version of the plan has been developed using the protocol Version 2.1 dated 10 AUG2023 and CRF
specifications dated 13Jul2023. Any further changes to the protocol or CRF will be reviewed for potential
impact on the SAP which will be amended if it is deemed necessary.
All versions of this plan will be reviewed by the Simbec-Orion project manager, medical writer and
statistical reviewer. The SAP will be finalised and approved by the Sponsor prior to database lock.
1.2 CHANGES FROM PROTOCOL
All Randomized Set has been added to analysis sets.
Progression-Free Survival (PFS) and Time to Progression (TTP) will both be analysed as secondary
endpoints instead of PFS or TTP. Definitions are included in this SAP.
Per Protocol set to be defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that could
potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoints.
Duration of Response (DoR) will be summarized by Kaplan-Meier estimate of the median with the
associated 95 % confidence interval and censoring will be occur in patients without progression or death
until EOS.
1.3 CHANGES FROM PREVIOUS VERSIONS OF THE SAP
Changes from SAP version 1.0:
- Updates have been made based on protocol amendment (v2.1 dated 10Aug2023) and eCRF
amendment (dated 13Jul2023).
- Summary tables for serious treatment-emergent adverse by relationship to VCN-01,
Gemcitabine and Nab-paclitaxel events have been added to the safety analysis.
- Definition of Per Protocol Set has been updated.
- Summary statistics for DoR have been added to use Kaplan-Meier estimate.
- Kaplan-Meier figures have been added to the time-to event endpoints.
Changes from SAP version 2.0:
- Updates on final TFLs shells.
- Kaplan-Meier figures for PFS (FAS), Subgroup analysis for OS and PFS (ITT) and for Duration of
Response (FAS) have been added to the efficacy analysis.
- Added demographic and baseline characteristics table to be summarized on Full Analysis Set
- Visit windowing and baseline definition for QoL outcomes have been updated. Baseline for
ECOG has been updated.
- Topline TFLs have been selected for the final TFL delivery.

2 STUDY OBJECTIVES
2.1 PRIMARY OBJECTIVES
This study will enroll patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer into one of two treatment arms (Arm I
or Arm II) as detailed in Section 3 Study Design. The primary objectives of the study are:
• To evaluate the time from randomization until death in both arms (Overall Survival)
• To evaluate the safety and tolerability of VCN-01, intravenously (IV) administered at Week 1
and Week 14 in Arm II (VCN-01 in combination with Nab-paclitaxel and Gemcitabine).
2.2 SECONDARY OBJECTIVES
The secondary objectives are:
• To evaluate the Time to Progression (TTP) and Progression-free Survival (PFS)
• To determine the Objective Response Rate (ORR)
• To determine the Disease Control Rate (DCR) (stable disease [SD] + partial response [PR] +
complete response [CR])
• To determine the landmark 1-year survival and PFS at the 1-year landmark
• To evaluate the Duration of Response (DoR)
• To assess changes in tumor marker carbohydrate antigen (Ca) 19.9 measured every 4 weeks
while on study.
2.3 EXPLORATORY OBJECTIVES
• To evaluate circulating immune markers in serum, VCN-01 genomes in blood, PH20 levels in
serum, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio, and serum levels of neutralizing anti-VCN-01 antibodies
(Anti-Ad-NAbs)
• To evaluate radiomic analysis of computerized tomography (CT) images
• To characterize the Quality of Life (QoL) via the validated European Organization for Research
and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC) QLQ-C30 questionnaire
(version 3)
• To determine the disease control rate (DCR) to the subsequent anticancer therapies.
3 STUDY DESIGN
3.1 OVERVIEW
This is a multi-center, open label, randomized, 2-parallel arm, phase IIb study of nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine as Standard of Care (SoC) plus/minus VCN-01 in patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer.
Approximately 92 patients in about 25 sites in North America (NA) and European Union (EU) will be
recruited and randomized in a 1:1 ratio to one of two treatment arms:

• Arm I: Nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine as SoC (28-day cycles). Patients in this arm will not receive
the Investigational Medicinal Product (IMP) (VCN-01).
• Arm II: Two (2) doses of VCN-01 administrated in combination with nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine as SoC (28-day cycles with exception of the IMP dose cycles, which will be 35-day
cycles).
The randomization will be stratified to take account of the patients’ baseline Eastern Cooperative
Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status (0 or 1) and region (NA or EU).
A Data Monitoring Committee (DMC) will be convened at regular intervals to assess safety and to look
at Overall Survival (OS) to determine if the trial can continue, as mentioned in the DMC charter.
See Section 16.1 for the Study Design.
3.2 INCLUSION AND EXCLUSION CRITERIA
To be eligible for inclusion into this study, each patient must fulfil all inclusion criteria and not violate
any exclusion criteria within 28 days up to and including Study Day 1 (first day of treatment with
IMP/SoC). Details of the inclusion and exclusion criteria are presented in the protocol and amendments.
3.3 STUDY TREATMENT
For this study, VCN-01 is considered an IMP while nab-paclitaxel and gemcitabine are considered non-
IMPs to be administrated as SoC.
Approximately 92 patients in about 25 sites in NA and EU will be recruited and randomized in a 1:1
ratio to one of the two treatment arms described above. Patients in both arms will continue study
treatment until progressive disease (PD), intolerable/unacceptable toxicity or patient’s/investigator’s
decision. This period will be defined as Treatment period.
3.4 STUDY TIMEPOINTS
The trial includes the following periods:
• Screening period (approximately 4 weeks prior to first dose): Days -28 to -1 (Week -4 to -1);
there is no Day 0
• Randomization can occur any time during the 28-day Screening period when all the screening
assessments are completed, but dosing (D1) must take place no later than 5 days after
randomization.
• Treatment period (variable, depending on progression of disease/toxicity and decision of
patient/investigator):
o Arm I: Cycle 1 (28 days); Cycle 2 (28 days); Cycle 3 (28 days); Cycle 4 (28 days) and
subsequent nab-paclitaxel / gemcitabine cycles
o Arm II: Cycle 1 (35 days); Cycle 2 (28 days); Cycle 3 (28 days); Cycle 4 (35 days) and
subsequent nab-paclitaxel / gemcitabine cycles
o End-of-Treatment (EOT) visit: 1 month after last dose (±1 week)
• Follow-up (FU) period:
o FU without PD (±1 week): every 4 weeks (q4wk) until PD
o FU due to PD (±1 week): q4wk during the first 6 months; every 2 months (q2mo) until
the second year; every 6 months (q6mo) after the second year

• End of Study (EOS): Patients will be followed for survival until the EOS regardless of further
treatments, or until the sponsor ends the study. Early trial termination of the study by the
Sponsor is only anticipated on the basis of safety.
See Protocol Appendix 7 and 8 for the Study Schedule in Arm I and Arm II.
3.5 SAMPLE SIZE CONSIDERATIONS
Assuming an accrual time of 18 months with (minimum) 12-month FU for all patients, 1-sided
alpha = 0.05, beta= 0.2 (80% power), the median OS=10.6 months for Arm I and the median OS=20.8
for Arm II with 1: 1 randomization, 46 patients would be needed for each study arm to reach the 57
events needed using the logrank test. It is therefore planned to randomize a total of 92 adult patients
with metastatic pancreatic cancer into the study for final analysis.
3.6 RANDOMIZATION
Patients will be randomized in a ratio of 1:1 to receive either SoC or SoC + 2 administrations of VCN-
01. The randomization will be stratified to take account of the patients’ baseline ECOG performance
status (0 or 1) and region (NA or EU).
4 STUDY VARIABLES AND COVARIATES
4.1 PRIMARY VARIABLES
The primary variables are:
• Overall Survival (OS)
• Safety and tolerability of VCN-01 in Arm II
4.2 SECONDARY VARIABLES
The secondary variables are:
• PFS or TTP
• ORR
• DCR (SD + PR + CR)
• Landmark 1-year survival and PFS at the 1-year landmark
• DoR
• Changes in tumor marker Ca 19.9
4.3 EXPLORATORY VARIABLES
The exploratory variables are:
• Biomarker levels, such as PH20, VCN-01 genomes, neutrophil/lymphocyte ratio, anti-Ad-NAb,
circulating immune markers and/or other markers according to the state of the art, may be
determined in blood and serum samples collected at different timepoints during the study.
• Image biomarkers (radiomics) assessed from the images of CT scans performed during the study.
• Change from baseline in values of the QoL via the validated EORTC QLQ-C30 questionnaire
(version 3).
• DCR (SD + PR + CR) to the subsequent therapies.

4.4 PHARMACOKINETIC VARIABLES
Pharmacokinetic variables are not evaluated in this study.
4.5 PHARMACODYNAMIC VARIABLES
Please refer to Section 4.3 for exploratory Pharmacodynamic variables. No further Pharmacodynamic
variables will be evaluated in this study.
4.6 SAFETY VARIABLES
Safety will be evaluated by the following:
• Demographics
• Medical history
• Prior medications and procedures, including standard of care
• Concomitant medications and procedures
• Physical examinations
• Vital signs assessments
• Safety laboratory test – biochemistry, hematology, coagulation profile, thyroid stimulating
hormone (TSH), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV)/Hepatitis C Virus (HCV), tuberculosis (TB) test and
Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV), urinalysis and pregnancy test
• 12-Lead electrocardiogram (ECG)
• COVID-19 testing
• Left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF)
• Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) score
• Fibroscan (if clinically indicated)
• Adverse event (AE)/serious adverse event (SAE) assessment.
5 DEFINITIONS
Study Drug: Study drug is taken to mean either VCN-01 (considered as IMP) or nab-paclitaxel and
gemcitabine (considered as non-IMPs to be administrated as SoC).
Baseline: Baseline is defined by patient and by variable as the last non-missing value (including
repeat/unscheduled assessments) before the first dose of study drug except for QoL and ECOG result.
The baseline for QoL is C1D1, if not missing, otherwise the closes value which is before C1D1. The
baseline ECOG status refers to the ECOG assessment used to determine stratification at randomization.
This is always the Screening value. Study Day: Study day is the number of days since start of treatment
where the date of first dose is counted as Day 1 (there is no Day 0).
Protocol Deviation: a deviation related to study inclusion or exclusion criteria, conduct of the trial,
patient management or patient assessment. This refers to any change, divergence, or departure from
the study design or procedures defined in the protocol. Protocol deviations captured in the CRF will be
reviewed on a regular basis during the study and discussed at the Data Review Meeting (DRM) before
Database Lock (DBL). In addition, any deviations identified during the DRM will be discussed and included
in the database as necessary. All protocol deviations within the study database will be classified as either
‘Major’ or ‘Minor’ prior to DBL, details of which will be included within the Protocol Deviations Listing.

6 ANALYSIS SETS
Membership of the analysis sets will be reviewed and agreed at a DRM before database lock.
6.1 ALL RANDOMIZED SET
The All Randomized Set is defined as all patients who are randomized.
This analysis set will be used for the summary of disposition.
6.2 SAFETY ANALYSIS SET (SAF)
The Safety Analysis Set (SAF) is defined as all patients who are randomized and take at least any dose of
Study Drug.
This analysis set will be used for demographic and safety summaries as well as for study listings. The
treatment arm is defined as the treatment that actually treated the patient.
6.3 INTENT-TO-TREAT SET (ITT)
The intent-to-treat (ITT) analysis set is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
any dose of Study Drug. The treatment arm is defined as the treatment that is randomized to treat the
patient.
The ITT will be used for demographic and baseline characteristics summary and for all efficacy analyses.
6.4 FULL ANALYSIS SET (FAS)
The Full Analysis Set (FAS) is defined as all patients who are randomized and have received
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose, if allocated to Arm 1 or
• at least 1/3 of the planned chemotherapy dose and a complete dose of VCN-01, if allocated to
Arm II
during the first cycle of the study.
The FAS will be used for the efficacy analyses of the primary and secondary variables and for demographic
and baseline characteristics.
6.5 PER-PROTOCOL SET (PPS)
The Per-Protocol Set (PPS) is defined as patients in the FAS without any major protocol deviations that
could potentially influence a primary or main secondary study endpoint.
Primary analysis will be repeated for the PPS.
6.6 PHARMACODYNAMIC SET (PDS)
The Pharmacodynamic Set (PDS) will consist of all patients in the FAS who had at least 1
pharmacodynamic measurement, had no major protocol deviations affecting pharmacodynamic
parameters and no deviation from pharmacodynamic sampling procedures.

7 SAFETY MONITORING
An independent DMC will be established to ensure patient safety, to consider patient risks against the
potential for meeting trial objectives, and to provide recommendations to the Sponsor with respect to
the conduct of the trial.
The DMC will perform the following major functions:
• The DMC will be responsible for the ongoing review of safety data throughout the trial. Primary
among the safety data to be reviewed will be SAEs, any adverse drug reactions and all relevant
available clinical laboratory data.
• The DMC may review acute and additional safety data, on a patient-by-patient basis, at their
discretion. This would be warranted if significant unexpected events are observed.
• The DMC may request additional safety data if, in the view of the committee, these additional
data are needed in order to make an informed, responsible decision about the conduct of the
trial.
• The DMC will advise the Sponsor regarding safety of patients and continuing validity and
scientific merit of the trial. The DMC will also monitor the number of deaths in both arms of
the study.
If emerging data from this unblinded study suggest that an interim analysis for futility or efficacy is
warranted, the clinical study protocol, DMC responsibilities, and this SAP may be amended to
incorporate such analysis.
All details of the conduct and responsibilities of the study DMC along with the frequency of DMC
meetings will be described in the ‘DMC Charter’, which will be finalized prior to the start of patient
enrolment.
8 INTERIM ANALYSES
No interim analysis is planned. If emerging data from this unblinded study suggest that an interim analysis
for futility or efficacy is warranted, the clinical study protocol, DMC responsibilities, and this SAP may
be amended to incorporate such analysis.

10 STATISTICAL METHODS
10.1 GENERAL PRINCIPLES

document “Statistical Principles for Clinical Trials”.

Data will be summarised by treatment arm. Where appropriate, data will also be summarised by visit
with summaries for each visit attended as scheduled and an additional summary for final (last scheduled
visit or early withdrawal). The format of the summaries is defined in the shells at the end of this
document.
In summary and analysis tables of continuous variables, standard descriptive statistics (N, mean, standard
deviation [STD], median, minimum and maximum) will be presented. Least squares mean (LS mean),
standard error (SE) and 95% confidence interval (CI) will be presented in the statistical analysis outputs
as appropriate. The minimum and maximum statistics will be presented in summary tables to the same
number of significant figures as the original data. The mean, median, LS mean, CI, STD and SE will be
presented to one more significant than the original data.
In summary tables of categorical variables, the number of non-missing observations by category will be
presented with percentages. Unless otherwise specified, the denominator for each percentage will be
the number of non-missing observations within the column. All percentages will be presented to one
decimal place.
If changes in severity for the same Treatment Emergent Adverse Event (TEAE) have been reported
separately but with the same AE number, they will be collapsed to a single AE with maximum severity
for the summary tables, but will be listed as reported.
Classifications of medical history, concomitant medication and adverse events will be sorted
alphabetically within the summary tables.
If any laboratory assessments are repeated at the same visit, the result from the repeat assessment will
be used in summaries. Both values will be listed.
Data collected on the eCRF will be presented within data listings. The data listings will be sorted by
treatment arm, patient number and visit. If any patients receive the wrong treatment this will be flagged
in all listings. For patients who complete the study, the last visit will be described in the listings as ‘<Cycle
X Day Y>’; for those who withdraw early it will be described as ‘End of Study’.
The date format for all output presentations will be ‘ddMMMyyyy’.
All statistical analysis will be performed using SAS® Enterprise Guide 8.3 or higher.
All hypothesis testing will be carried out at the 5% (2-sided) significance level unless stated otherwise.
P-values will be rounded to four decimal places. P-values less than 0.0001 will be reported as <0.0001
in tables.
If any of the assumptions underlying the formal statistical methods proposed are violated during the
analysis of the final data, alternative statistical methods will be used and any changes documented in the
statistical methods section of the CSR, including the rationale for use.
10.2 STRATIFICATION AND COVARIATE ADJUSTMENT
Randomization is stratified by ECOG (=0 or =1) at baseline and region (=NA or =EU). The primary
analysis will be adjusted for the stratification factors.
10.3 INTERACTIONS
No interactions are to be performed.

10.4 MISSING DATA
There will be no imputation of missing data in this study.
10.5 POOLING OF SITES
Sites will be pooled for all analyses. There will be no adjustment for centre effect or treatment by centre
interaction.
10.6 MULTIPLE COMPARISONS
A sequential testing will be used to control the overall false positive rate at the 5% (2-sided) significance
level for the primary and secondary variables, based on the ITT analysis set. Specifically, the primary
variable (OS) will be tested first. If the P-value for OS is < 0.05, then the secondary variables will be
tested in the order that is listed in the SAP. The PFS will be tested first. If the P-value for PFS is < 0.05,
then ORR will be tested next. If at anytime the P-value is > 0.05, the testing procedure will stop.
10.7 SUBGROUP ANALYSES
Analyses for the primary endpoint (OS) and the main secondary endpoints (PFS, TTP and ORR) will be
repeated for the following subgroup:
- Arm I: patients who had the first 3 cycles of SoC chemotherapy and started the 4th SoC
chemotherapy
- Arm II: patients who had the first 3 cycles of SoC chemotherapy, started the 4th cycle of SoC
chemotherapy and received 2 doses of VCN-01.
Subgroup analyses will be performed using the ITT. Subgroup analysis will also be performed for the
primary endpoint using the PPS.

11.1 PATIENT DISPOSITION
Information about screening failures will be provided by the project manager and presented in the CSR

11.3.1 Primary Variable
11.3.1.1 Overall Survival (OS)
The primary efficacy endpoint is survival time (OS), defined as time from randomization until death.

A Cox Proportional Hazards model will be fitted to the data with the Cox adjustment for tied
observations. Model terms will include region, baseline ECOG performance status and treatment. A

provided. Analysis will be performed using the ITT (Table 14.2.1.1) and will be repeated using the FAS
and PPS (Table 14.2.1.2 and Table 14.2.1.3). Subgroup analysis will also be performed for patients defined
under section 10.7 for ITT (Table 14.2.1.4) and for PPS (Table 14.2.1.5).

(Figure 14.2.1 - Figure 14.2.3). Subgroup analysis will also be performed and Kaplan-Meier curve will be
plotted (Figure 14.2.4).

Scoring of the QLQ-C30 questionnaire:
The QLQ-C30 is composed of both multi-item scales and single-item measures. These include five
functional scales, three symptom scales, a global health status / QoL scale, and six single items. Each of
the multi-item scales includes a different set of items - no item occurs in more than one scale. A summary
of the scales can be found in the following figure.
All of the scales and single-item measures range in score from 0 to 100. A high scale score represents a
higher response level. Thus a high score for a functional scale represents a high / healthy level of
functioning, a high score for the global health status / QoL represents a high QoL, but a high score for a
symptom scale / item represents a high level of symptomatology / problems.
The principle for scoring these scales is the same in all cases:
1. 2. Estimate the average of the items that contribute to the scale; this is the raw score.
Use a linear transformation to standardise the raw score, so that scores range from 0 to 100; a
higher score represents a higher ("better") level of functioning, or a higher ("worse") level of
symptoms.

medicinal product (IMP) that are definitely related to any IMP dose administered. Serious Adverse

caused death if it were more severe)
• Requires in-patient hospitalisation or prolongation of existing hospitalization
• Results in persistent or significant disability/incapacity
• Is a congenital anomaly/birth defect
• Is a significant medical/surgical event, e.g. an event that jeopardises the patient or requires
intervention to prevent one of the above outcomes.
